intended_object: This is a helper map used in the proof. It is the radial interpolation H : I × (U ∩ V) → U ∩ V on the intersection of the two punctured-circle charts. H(0, ·) sends each point to a chosen representative of its component, and H(1, ·) is the identity. I inferred this from the docstring and from the lemmas that come right after it.
explanation: The definition only bundles the existing function `circlePunctureIntersectionRadialPoint` and the proof that it is continuous into a `ContinuousMap` on `unitInterval × circlePunctureIntersection`. It exists to supply a homotopy, used in the proof that the intersection of the punctured circles deformation retracts onto a discrete set of component representatives. It has no standalone counterpart in the mathematical literature. It does match its docstring: the lemmas `circlePunctureIntersectionRadialPoint_zero` and `circlePunctureIntersectionRadialPoint_one`, stated right after it, give the time-0 and time-1 behaviour the docstring describes.
